transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Lately I just can’t think straight or make decisions at work the way I used to. It’s gotten to the point where it’s really affecting my job at the warehouse, and a colleague suggested I should come in and get some help.
Did these problems start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without an obvious trigger?

Well, I've had these ups and downs off and on for a couple of years, but they really came to a head this past year. It all started when I was shortlisted for a regional director job at work, which brought on a ton of pressure, longer hours, and a lot of supervisor turnover to deal with.
Have these symptoms mostly been tied to that work stress, and do they improve when the stress eases, or have they continued even during calmer periods?

While the work stress this past year made everything a lot worse, these ups and downs have actually been happening for at least a couple of years, even when things were calmer. Even my primary doctor noticed that it seemed like a longstanding pattern of mood shifts rather than just normal burnout from my job.

During those ups and downs, have you had periods of several days or more where your mood was unusually low or unusually upbeat/irritable, with changes in energy, sleep, or activity? Or has it mainly been a persistent low mood or stress-related difficulty without clear episodes?

Yes, I definitely have clear "up" and "down" periods rather than just a flat line. During the highs, I feel completely wired and snappy, staying up until 2 AM to work on my motorcycle and taking on way too many tasks at work. But then I'll crash into a low slump like this current one, which has been dragging on since last fall and makes me feel completely slowed down.
Have the low periods ever lasted at least 2 weeks, and do they happen even when there is no major stressor at work or in your life?

Yes, they definitely last much longer than two weeks—this current low spell has been dragging on since last fall, so it's been nearly a year. These ups and downs have actually been happening off and on for at least a couple of years, even during times when things were much calmer at work.
When you are in those low or high periods, do they happen only after a stressful event and then improve as the stress passes, or do they come on and persist even when life is relatively calm?

They definitely come on and persist even when life is relatively calm. While the recent stress from trying to get that regional director role made these shifts much worse, I've actually been experiencing these alternating high and low periods off and on for at least a couple of years, well before that intense pressure started.
During your high periods, do you ever have symptoms like needing much less sleep, feeling unusually confident or grand, talking more than usual, racing thoughts, or doing risky things?

Yes, I experience almost all of those during my high periods. My mind races so fast that I jump from one idea to the next, and I can stay up working on my bike until 2 AM without feeling tired at all. I also get this unrealistic confidence where I think I could run the whole region better than corporate, and I'll do risky things like driving way too fast at night or putting big purchases on my credit card.
During your low periods, do you also have symptoms like feeling hopeless, losing interest or pleasure, changes in appetite or sleep, guilt, or thoughts of death or suicide?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in fishing or working on my bike, and I often have to remind myself to eat because I have no appetite. When I make a mistake at work, I feel like a complete failure as a husband, father, and boss, and on the really bad days, I've had dark thoughts about not waking up or even driving my truck into a wall.
During your high or low periods, have you ever had hallucinations or strongly believed things that other people said were not true?

No, I’ve never had anything like that happen. Even though my mood swings can get pretty extreme, I’ve never seen or heard things that aren’t there, and I’ve never believed things that other people told me were completely unreal.

Right now, are you feeling mostly depressed, or have you had a period of at least several days recently where you felt unusually energized, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or active than usual?

Right now, I am definitely feeling very low and depressed, and this slump has been dragging on since last fall. But before this, I definitely had those revved-up phases where I had endless energy, stayed up late working on projects without feeling tired, and just couldn't sit still.

Have you ever had a high period that lasted at least 1 week and caused major problems at work, with symptoms like needing very little sleep, feeling unusually energized or confident, and being more impulsive than usual?

Yes, those high periods usually last for a week or more, and I'd run on an "extra battery" working on my bike until 2 AM, buying expensive tools, and feeling so confident I thought I could run the whole region better than corporate. It definitely caused issues at work because I'd take on too many projects with this overzealous initiative. A colleague actually warned me that my leadership had become unpredictable because I'd swing from that high state back down to being completely disengaged.

Have you had any periods during this current low mood where you were able to enjoy things at all, or has the depression been so severe that you feel almost no pleasure or energy most of the day nearly every day?

The depression has been so severe that I feel almost no pleasure or energy at all. I can't even enjoy working on my motorcycle or planning fishing trips anymore; I just stare at my tools or fishing rod, feel absolutely nothing, and end up sitting on the couch. My energy is so low that I move very slowly, shuffling around the house and feeling like it takes forever just to get my body going.
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself or hurting yourself, and if so, do you have any plan or intention to act on them?

I do catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be so terrible if I just didn’t wake up one morning. On the really rough days, I’ve even pictured driving my truck into a wall, but I don’t have any actual plans or intention to do it.

During your high periods, do you ever become so energized or irritable that you need hospitalization, or have you had major consequences like getting fired, getting into fights, or making very dangerous decisions because of it?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, fired, or gotten into any physical fights during those times. But I do make some risky decisions, like driving way too fast on the highway at night, overspending on credit cards for tools without telling my wife, and snapping at people at work and home when I get irritable.
Have you ever had a high period so severe that you needed to be hospitalized, or that it caused you to become unable to function at work or at home because of the mood episode itself?

No, I've never been hospitalized for a high period. During those 'on' times, I actually felt like I had extra energy and was doing way too much, like working late and tinkering on projects, though I did do some impulsive things like speeding and overspending. It is really the low periods where I truly struggle to function.
Have you ever had a period of feeling so energized or irritable that you needed to be hospitalized, or that others said you were completely out of control or not yourself?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized, but people close to me definitely noticed I was acting differently during those high times. My wife would complain that I couldn’t sit still, and a colleague pointed out that my behavior was unpredictable because I'd get too overzealous, drive too fast, and spend too much money on tools.
Have you ever had a high period so severe that you were hospitalized, or that it caused you to become unable to function at work or at home because of the episode itself?

No, I've never been hospitalized for those high periods because during those times I actually felt like I was functioning at a very high level, working extra shifts and starting new projects. Even though I did some impulsive things like speeding or overspending, it is really the low periods that make me struggle to function and pull away from my work and family.
Have your high periods ever lasted at least 4 days but less than a week, or do they usually last a full week or more?

I'm not completely sure of the exact number of days, but those high or "on" periods usually seem to last for about a week or so at a time. I've never really tracked the exact days closely, but they definitely linger for a while before I slump back down.
Have your low periods lasted at least 2 weeks and been severe enough to cause major problems with work, sleep, appetite, or taking care of yourself?

Yes, they last much longer than two weeks—this current slump has been dragging on since last fall, and I often completely forget to eat because I have no appetite. It’s caused huge problems at work because my head feels full of mud, making it so hard to make simple decisions that I’ve missed deadlines and had to hand off my supervisor reviews.
During your low periods, do your symptoms make it very hard to work, take care of yourself, or function day to day, or are you still able to manage most of your usual responsibilities?

Yes, they make it extremely difficult to function. I've missed deadlines at work, had to hand off my supervisor reviews, and completely pulled back from church and family gatherings because I feel too unreliable to show up. Even simple things like moving around the house or making basic decisions feel like trying to push through thick mud.
Have you ever had a low period this severe that you became unable to function at all or needed hospitalization, or had any hallucinations or fixed false beliefs during the depression?

No, I have never been hospitalized, nor have I ever heard voices, seen things, or had any strange beliefs. However, while I've never been completely unable to function, these low periods—especially this current one dragging on since last fall—have still been severe enough to make me miss work deadlines, pull away from my family and church, and even have dark thoughts about driving my truck into a wall.
Have you ever had a depressive episode so severe that you were unable to function at all or needed hospitalization, or had any hallucinations or fixed false beliefs during the depression?

No, I've never been hospitalized, and I've never had any hallucinations or false beliefs during these depressions. But even though it hasn't gotten that extreme, it's still caused huge problems like missing work deadlines, handing off my supervisor reviews, and pulling away from church and family because I feel too unreliable to show up.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports bipolar I disorder with the current episode being severe depression without psychotic features. He has a clear history of manic episodes lasting about a week or more, with decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, inflated self-confidence/grandiosity, increased goal-directed activity, irritability, impulsive spending and risky driving, causing occupational and interpersonal problems. He is currently in a prolonged major depressive episode with marked anhedonia, psychomotor slowing, appetite loss, impaired concentration, functional impairment, and passive suicidal ideation, without psychosis. The depressive episode is severe, but he denies hospitalization and there is no evidence of psychotic symptoms.
